To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the eigenspace restructuring principle is a principle of space and frequency in neural networks, (2) it improves learnability, (3) it can be used to understand the power and the limitations of convolutional networks, (4) it can be applied to improve the learnability of MLPs by increasing their depth.

(i) the concept space and the concept frequency together form the basis of the eigenstructure of CNNs, (ii) this eigenstructure dramatically improves CNNs’ learnability, and (iii) the learnability improves further with increasing depth.

(1) CNNs restructure the eigenspaces of neural kernels into finer subspaces; (2) The finer subspaces are determined by both concept frequency and concept space; and (3) The depth of a CNN controls the resolution of the concept space.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions:

the following questions. How does the structure of the input space affect the structure of the associated eigenspace? What is the effect of such structure on the learnability of neural networks? How does the depth of a neural network affect its learnability?
a new principle of space and frequency in deep neural networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CNNs are able to learn more efficiently by reorganizing the eigenspaces of their infinite-width kernels in an optimal manner.
CNNs are better at interpolating and extrapolating, while MLPs are better at modeling interactions.
CNNs are better at modeling the interactions in the input space, and deeper CNNs are better than shallower CNNs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CNNs are better than MLPs in learning long-range-low-frequency and short-range-high-frequency concepts, and that increasing the depth can improve the resolution.
CNNs are a natural way to restructure the eigenspaces of MLPs to improve the network’s learnable capacity, while maintaining their locality and hierarchical structure.
, in the infinite-width limit, the learnability of a network is proportional to the number of concept spaces it can resolve, which is in turn proportional to its depth and frequency range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hierarchical locality principle is a powerful mechanism for learning a richer class of interactions in neural networks.
the structure of the eigenspace can play a key role in understanding the success of neural networks.

the success of CNNs is not due to their locality but rather to their restructuring of the eigenspaces of infinite-width MLPs into finer subspaces that enable them to better learn long-range interactions, which are crucial in many tasks.
